steps.what: Identify patron, materials and requested circulation transaction
Enter routine reservations, renewals and discharge transactions
Resolve circulation exceptions and hand over materials or receipts

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} library system to execute eligible transactions directly from staff capture. Keep identification, scanning, physical handover and exception resolution with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate capture and confirmation screens can require repeated entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native circulation policies can apply deterministic eligibility and due-date rules.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed returns, damaged materials and patron access problems.
tasks.human_edge: The technician resolves exceptions fairly and handles the physical materials.
tasks.altitude: Less routine transaction entry with unchanged patron service responsibility.

evidence.claim: Native library circulation rules can remove duplicate transaction entry where staff currently perform it; this is an E1 workflow scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers staff-mediated circulation; no saving from replacing patron effort or physical movement.

Technician produces transaction capture in s1: patron identifier, item barcode, action, timestamp and requested renewal or reservation. Its 40 hours include scanning, action selection and correcting unreadable barcodes. Missing identifiers are entered manually there.

Library manager maintains existing circulation policy: eligibility, loan period, renewal cap and hold priority. Additional technician rule tests take 5 hours and librarian policy review 2 hours per 100 focal baseline hours.

Test native scan-to-transaction settings first. Only existing manual re-entry in s2 earns a saving; existing automated runtime earns none. If s2 is already automatic, use zero gross saving and do not build.
unknowns: Current number of confirmation and re-entry screens
research_questions: Does scan-to-transaction remove 35 of 100 technician hours without increasing capture or exception time?

incremental.description: Test circulation rules and monitor failed transactions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+25=65; gross 35 less 5 upkeep gives net 30. High assumes all s2 is duplicate manual entry; low applies where existing automation leaves no implementable saving and deployment is declined. Physical and patron work retain time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify routine reference inquiries and capture the patron question
Consult reference sources for a supported answer

loop.purpose: Suggest a short answer from retrieved source passages
loop.input: Captured question and retrieved reference passages with record identifiers
loop.output: Answer draft with passage links and unresolved questions
loop.check: Technician reads passages to check that the answer addresses the actual question and preserves limitations; code verifies record links resolve
loop.stop: One search revision, then manual lookup or referral if sources do not support the answer
loop.why_not_simpler: Reference questions and source wording vary; exact keyword matching alone does not establish relevance

steps.what: Answer the patron or refer to a librarian

tasks.design: Offer a source-linked draft from the {OTHER} library discovery system. The technician checks its meaning, answers personally and refers uncertain or specialist questions to a librarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference lookup crosses catalogue entries and source passages.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked reference answer drafting is available; it still needs relevance checking.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the patron's real question and recognising inadequate sources.
tasks.human_edge: The technician clarifies intent and avoids confidently repeating unsupported references.
tasks.altitude: More lookup assistance without transferring the patron conversation.

reach.learn: Research question framing and source evaluation

evidence.claim: Primo Research Assistant answers reference questions from the top five abstracts with source links. This supports a bounded discovery capability, not comprehensive reference accuracy or the proposed time saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes clarification, lookup and answer, excluding the librarian's subsequent specialist investigation.

Technician captures question text, requested material type and scope in s1; its unchanged 30 hours include any typing. Existing cataloguers produce catalogue identifiers, abstracts and source links during normal cataloguing; no new metadata enrichment is assumed.
Missing abstracts or inaccessible sources trigger manual lookup within s2, never fabricated citations.
Test native catalogue search and saved reference resources before adding a draft loop.
Five technician upkeep hours and two librarian source-review hours are additional per 100 focal baseline hours.
research_questions: Do checked drafts reduce lookup time after question entry and failed searches?

already_counted.description: Check draft support and perform fallback searches

incremental.description: Review failures and update reference coverage

approvals.approved_version: Exact answer wording and source passages checked immediately before delivery; substantive changes require another check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+21+35=86; gross 14 less 5 upkeep gives net 9. Low 2 allows seven extra hours for abstract gaps and manual searches. Conversation and referral delivery stay unchanged; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Process print and non-print materials for inclusion in collections

tasks.design: Keep labelling, covering and physical preparation with the technician. Existing processing instructions in {DOCS} remain available; no extra administrative baseline is introduced to create a software saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials require physical inspection and handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital instructions can support consistent work but do not perform it.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual formats and fragile materials need care.
tasks.human_edge: The technician adapts treatment to the physical item.
tasks.altitude: Preparation time and responsibility are unchanged.

reach.task: Agree handling requirements for unusual formats

evidence.claim: Digital record tools do not replace manual covering and physical preparation of library items.

assumptions: Boundary is physical preparation; descriptive cataloguing belongs to the separate cataloguing task.
No structured feed or machine action is introduced. Technician observes item condition while doing the full-time preparation.
Check existing instructions before building anything.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new workflow or software is deployed.
unknowns: Mix of physical and digital materials
research_questions: Which observed preparation operations are actually software entry rather than physical handling?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. Physical preparation remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Catalogue books and other materials from their identifying pages

loop.purpose: Suggest descriptive catalogue fields from captured title-page evidence
loop.input: Item title-page image or manually entered title and author
loop.output: Draft description with field evidence and uncertain matches
loop.check: Technician compares title, author, edition, format and subject meaning to the actual item; controlled headings are checked against the local vocabulary
loop.stop: One corrected match attempt, then manual cataloguing for uncertain editions or unsupported fields
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact shared-record copying is preferred; unmatched items need interpretation of varied title pages

steps.what: Check the catalogue entry and assign its storage designation
Sort materials and return them to designated shelves or files

tasks.design: Use native shared-record copying in the {OTHER} library catalogue first and a bounded metadata draft only for unmatched items. The technician accepts the final description and location, then physically sorts and shelves the materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unmatched editions require manual description and classification checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata draft tools can propose records from title-page evidence for cataloguer correction.
tasks.still_hard: Edition ambiguity, local classification and accurate shelving.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks the actual item and places it correctly.
tasks.altitude: Less initial description entry with unchanged acceptance and shelving time.

reach.learn: Controlled vocabulary and local classification policy

evidence.claim: Alma AI Metadata Assistant drafts a record from title, author or a title-page photo for cataloguer acceptance, correction or rejection.

assumptions: Boundary covers descriptive cataloguing, location assignment and sorting/shelving; physical covering is owned by the separate preparation task.

Technician produces title-page image or title, author and edition transcription within s1. Its remaining 21 hours include capture, matching, draft checking and manual fallback, rather than assuming free source preparation.
Technician produces the accepted item identifier, edition, call number and location in s2; physical sorting consumes that designation in s3. Uncertain locations are resolved manually before shelving.
Test native copy cataloguing and authority lists before adding a model draft.
Four technician upkeep hours and two librarian vocabulary-review hours are additional per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Do metadata drafts save time after title-page capture and edition checking on unmatched items?

already_counted.description: Capture evidence and correct metadata drafts

incremental.description: Monitor metadata failures and update mappings
Maintain heading policy for draft use

approvals.approved_version: Exact item identifier, edition, descriptive fields, headings, call number and location; any edit requires renewed acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=21+15+50=86; gross 14 less 4 upkeep gives net 10. Low 2 allows eight extra hours of capture and edition correction. Sorting and shelving retain all 50 hours; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Assist record and reference work while retaining patron contact, material care and shelving.
reach: Help librarians analyse reference and circulation exceptions
role.ambitious_version: A technician with less repeated entry and clear responsibility for reliable patron service.
